selected.label: chemrof:Reaction
selected.en: When curating a Reaction record, you must adhere to a strict data model that prohibits any unlisted properties, with the sole exception of the standard system type. Every reaction must specify exactly one string-based identifier. Beyond this required ID, the record may optionally include a single string representing the name of the chemical entity, such as nickel or carbon-16, as well as a single type designation. To capture the chemical transformation, you may provide at most one Proposed Reactions InChI representation and a single reaction SMILES representation. Furthermore, kinetic data can be recorded by optionally including a single floating-point value for the reaction rate and at most one floating-point value for the reaction rate coefficient.

selected.label: chemrof:Material
selected.en: When curating a Material, defined as a substance composed of repeated chemical units that has a specific arrangement of atoms or molecules, the data model must be strictly closed, permitting no outside properties other than the standard system type. Every material record must specify exactly one string-based identifier. In addition to this required identifier, the record may optionally include up to one string name, such as nickel or carbon-16, and at most one specific type designation. Finally, the material may feature a maximum of one repeat unit, which must be represented as a direct link to a recognized chemical entity.

selected.label: chemrof:ChemicalEntity
selected.en: When defining a chemical entity, which represents a discrete structure of one or more atoms describable by a chemical formula, the data model is open, allowing additional properties beyond the specified rules while explicitly ignoring system type declarations. Each entity must specify exactly one string-based identifier. It may also include at most one string-based name, such as nickel or carbon-16, and at most one string-based IUPAC name. To describe its structure, you may provide at most one empirical formula denoting the relative proportion of atoms, like CH2O for glucose. The entity can also include at most one InChI string and at most one InChI chemical sublayer; this sublayer acts as the main chemical formula and must be a string consisting exclusively of uppercase letters, numbers, and periods. Additionally, the entity may feature one or more SMILES strings, which encode the molecular graph without chiral or isotopic information, acknowledging that multiple valid SMILES can represent the same structure, just as CCO, OCC, and C(O)C all specify ethanol. A single boolean value can be provided to indicate whether the entity is a radical. The entity can have at most one type designation and at most one chemical role, with the role structured as an internal nested record. Finally, the entity may be hierarchically categorized under at most one parent class, also formatted as an internal nested record. In this model, these parent classes often act as metaclasses representing groupings or specific countable elements, allowing the entity to be connected either as a subtype of a broader grouping, like an alkane being a hydrocarbon, or classified directly into a grouping, such as methane being a hydrocarbon.

selected.label: chemrof:AtomGroupingByPeriodicTablePlacement
selected.en: When curating an atom grouping by periodic table placement, the data model is open, meaning additional properties beyond the core requirements are permitted. Every record must specify exactly one string-based identifier. The grouping can also provide at most one string-based name to describe the chemical entity, such as nickel or carbon-16. To establish hierarchical categorizations, the record may include up to one OWL subclass relationship, formatted as an internal nested record, which connects the entity to a broader class or metaclass. Furthermore, the grouping may define its specialization using the subtype of relationship. If provided, this must be a direct link to a specific molecule grouping class, indicating that the current entity is a more specialized form of that broader grouping.

selected.label: chemrof:SupramolecularPolymer
selected.en: When defining a supramolecular polymer—described as a polymeric array of monomeric units connected by reversible and highly directional secondary interactions, namely non-covalent bonds—the data model is strictly closed, meaning no outside properties are permitted other than standard system types. Each record must specify exactly one string identifier. Additionally, the record may include at most one string for its general name, at most one formal IUPAC name string, and at most one general type designation. The chemical nature of the polymer can be further detailed with at most one boolean value indicating whether it is a radical, and at most one empirical formula denoting the relative proportion of its atoms. For structural representation, the record may contain at most one complete InChI string, alongside specific InChI components: at most one main chemical formula sublayer that must consist exclusively of uppercase letters, numbers, and periods, and at most one atom connections sublayer detailing non-hydrogen bond connections, which must strictly begin with the lowercase letter c. The model also permits SMILES strings to encode the molecular graph without chiral or isotopic information. To define its composition and function, the polymer may feature at most one direct link to a specific macromolecule it is a polymer of, and at most one direct link to a chemical entity representing its repeat unit. Finally, its function and classification can be captured using at most one internal nested record defining its chemical role, and at most one internal nested record hierarchically categorizing it under a broader grouping or metaclass.

selected.label: chemrof:MolecularSubsequence
selected.en: When defining a molecular subsequence, the data model is strictly closed, meaning no outside properties are permitted other than standard system types. Every molecular subsequence must specify exactly one string identifier. Beyond this required identifier, the record may include an optional single string for the name of the chemical entity, an optional single string for its IUPAC name, an optional single boolean flag indicating whether the structure is a radical, and an optional single type designation. For structural representation, the model allows an optional single empirical formula denoting the relative proportion of atoms, as well as any number of SMILES strings that encode the molecular graph without chiral or isotopic information. You may also include an optional single complete InChI string. If detailing specific InChI components, you can provide an optional single string for the InChI chemical sublayer representing the main chemical formula, which must consist exclusively of uppercase letters, numbers, and periods. Additionally, an optional single string can be provided for the InChI atom connections sublayer; this must begin with the lowercase letter 'c' and describes how non-hydrogen atoms are sequentially numbered and connected by bonds. Finally, the structure supports complex relationships through internal nested records: an optional single unnamed structure can be used to assign a specific chemical role, and another optional single internal nested record can establish hierarchical categorizations, linking the subsequence to broader grouping classes or metaclasses.

selected.label: chemrof:ChemicalGroupingByCharge
selected.en: When curating a chemical grouping by charge, which serves as a grouping class that refines a charge-neutral entity, the data model is strictly closed, meaning no outside properties are permitted other than explicitly ignored system types. Each record must specify exactly one identifier as a text string. It may also include up to one name for the chemical entity, such as nickel or carbon-16, formatted as a string. To arrange these grouping classes into arbitrarily deep hierarchies, the record can include subtype relationships, which must be direct links or specific identifiers pointing to a molecule grouping class, ensuring this connection only occurs between two grouping classes. Finally, the entity may have at most one subclass relationship, represented as an internal nested record or unnamed structure categorized under an OWL class, which is used to establish hierarchical relationships where metaclasses represent groupings or specific countable elements.

selected.label: chemrof:SequenceInterval
selected.en: When defining a sequence interval, which represents a chain of connected monomers in a linear polymer such as a sub-region of an amino acid or nucleotide sequence, the data model is flexible and open, allowing additional properties beyond the standard constraints while ignoring standard system types. Every sequence interval must specify exactly one string-based identifier. You may optionally provide at most one string-based name for the chemical entity, such as nickel or carbon-16, as well as a single string-based IUPAC name. The interval can be flagged by at most one boolean value indicating if it is a radical, and it may define at most one chemical role, which must be provided as an internal nested record categorized under the Chemical Role class. For structural representation, you may include at most one sequence representation, a single standard InChI string, and at most one empirical formula, which denotes the relative proportion of atoms like CH2O for glucose. The model also permits SMILES strings, which encode the molecular graph without chiral or isotopic information. If detailing specific InChI components, you may provide at most one InChI chemical sublayer to represent the main chemical formula, which must be a string containing only uppercase letters, numbers, and periods. Additionally, you can include at most one InChI atom connections sublayer, which describes the bond connectivity between sequentially numbered non-hydrogen atoms; this must be a string that begins with a lowercase 'c'. Finally, the sequence interval may include at most one general type designation and at most one hierarchical subclass relationship, formatted as an internal nested record, to connect the specific element to a broader grouping or metaclass.

selected.label: PersonGenderShape
selected.en: The gender of a person must be Male, Female, or Other.

selected.label: FilmRatingShape
selected.en: A film's rating must be an integer between 1 and 5.

selected.label: BlogPostShape
selected.en: A blog post must have at least one tag.

selected.label: CityShape
selected.en: The name of a city must not exceed 100 characters.

selected.label: CountryShape
selected.en: A country code must be exactly two uppercase letters.

selected.label: BookISBNShape
selected.en: A book's ISBN must be a string.

selected.label: PersonHeightShape
selected.en: A person's height must be a positive decimal number.

selected.label: skos:Concept
selected.en: When defining a Concept, which represents a specific idea, notion, or unit of thought within the catalog, you must provide at least one preferred label. To ensure proper formatting, this preferred label must be recorded as a literal text value rather than a web link or identifier. Any violation of these constraints is considered a validation error and will be reported with a severity level of violation.

selected.label: spdx:Checksum
selected.en: When defining a Checksum, you must specify exactly one algorithm used to produce the checksum, and this must be provided as a specific identifier URL. Additionally, you must provide exactly one checksum value, which represents the actual lower case hexadecimal encoded digest produced by that algorithm, and this must be recorded as a literal text value. Any violation of these requirements is considered a validation error and will be reported with a severity level of violation.

selected.label: dct:LicenseDocument
selected.en: When cataloging a License Document, which serves as a legal document giving official permission to use a resource, you may specify at most one type to define the nature or genre of the license. If this type is provided, it must be expressed as a specific identifier URL that links to a standardized concept. Any violation of these requirements is considered a validation error and will be reported with a severity level of violation. Furthermore, to comply with strict license type restrictions, this concept must be explicitly categorized within a formal concept scheme. Specifically, it must contain at least one direct link indicating it belongs to the exact ADMS license type vocabulary located at http://purl.org/adms/licencetype/1.0.

selected.label: MandatoryCatalog
selected.en: When structuring your data catalog environment, it is strictly required to define at least one Catalog. Serving as a curated collection of metadata about resources like datasets and data services, the Catalog is a fundamental entity. To comply with this mandatory rule, your overall metadata submission must contain at least one explicit record that is formally classified as a Catalog.

selected.label: dcat:Catalog-1
selected.en: When defining a Catalog, which serves as a curated collection of metadata about resources, several constraints apply.   The catalog must include at least one title and at least one description, both provided as text. It is also required to specify exactly one publisher responsible for making the resource available, which must be provided as a specific identifier URL. Furthermore, the catalog must list at least one dataset. If you choose to record the dates when the catalog was formally issued or last modified, you may provide at most one of each, and they must be formatted strictly as either a date or a date-time value.   The catalog can be structured hierarchically, meaning it may be included in at most one parent catalog, while any parts of a catalog must also be catalogs. It may also include catalog records that describe the registration of individual datasets or data services.   For legal and informational purposes, the catalog can link to at most one license document giving official permission for its use, at most one rights statement detailing intellectual property rights, and at most one homepage document. Finally, any specified languages, spatial coverage characteristics, or theme taxonomies used to classify the datasets must be provided as specific identifier URLs.  Any violation of the specified constraints results in a validation error with severity level Violation

selected.label: dcat:Distribution-1
selected.en: When defining a Distribution, which serves as a specific physical or digital representation of a dataset, you must provide at least one access URL as an identifier URL to ensure the resource can be reached. The distribution's title and description, if provided, must be expressed as literal text values.  To track its lifecycle, if provided, at most one date issued and at most one date modified are allowed, and they must be formatted strictly as either a date or a date-time value. If you provide a download URL for the file, it must be an identifier URL.  If provided, the file's format must be given as at most one identifier URL referring to a Media Type or Extent. Similarly, if provided, at most one media type is allowed and it must refer to a Media Type or Extent.  If provided, the distribution's byte size must be a decimal number with at most one value.  For legal and access governance, if provided, at most one license is allowed, which must be a License Document, and at most one rights statement is allowed.  If indicating an established standard the distribution conforms to, it must be provided as either an identifier URL or an internal nested record. Additionally, if provided, the language of the resource must refer to a Linguistic System, and any related web pages must refer to Documents.  To verify file integrity, if provided, at most one checksum is allowed.  Finally, if provided, the distribution's status of the distribution must be represented by at most one identifier URL referring to a Concept with at most one value.  Any violation of these constraints results in a validation error with severity level Violation.

selected.label: MandatoryDataset
selected.en: When curating your data catalog, it is mandatory to include at least one Dataset. A Dataset represents a collection of data that is published or curated by a single source and made available for access or download in one or more representations. To satisfy this strict structural requirement, the data graph must contain at least one specific instance explicitly declared as a Dataset.

selected.label: foaf:Agent
selected.en: When defining an Agent, which represents an entity such as a person, group, software, or physical artifact, you must provide at least one name as a literal text value. You may also specify a maximum of one type. If a type is provided, it must be formatted as a specific identifier URL that represents a concept. Furthermore, this type concept is subject to a publisher type restriction, meaning it must be explicitly included in a concept scheme via a specific identifier URL, and this scheme must specifically be the ADMS publisher type 1.0 scheme. Any violation of these constraints results in a validation error with severity level Violation.

selected.label: epo-shape:epo-ord-ContractInformationShape
selected.en: When defining Contract Information to capture details about a contract, the record must include exactly one direct link to the specific Contract it concerns. This linked Contract represents the voluntary, deliberate, and legally binding agreement between competent parties and relates to the contractor. Additionally, the contract information may include direct links to specific Order Lines to capture information that is particular to one or multiple order lines. Any referenced Order Line must be provided as a specific identifier URL that details a given unit of goods, services, or works requested in the order.

selected.label: epo-shape:epo-QualityTargetInformationShape
selected.en: When defining Quality Target Information to capture details about a specific performance goal, the record must satisfy three specific requirements. It must contain exactly one direct link to a Contract Term, which establishes the conditions and stipulations defining particularities of the post-award phase. Additionally, the record requires exactly one specific identifier URL for the quality target code, pointing to a standardized concept that classifies the type of performance goal. Finally, it must include exactly one quality target description providing explanatory text about the performance goal, and this description must be formatted as either a standard text string or a language-tagged string.

selected.label: epo-shape:epo-CertificateShape
selected.en: When defining a Certificate, which serves as proof of conformance to a defined set of criteria to provide assurance of credibility, trust, and transparency in the procurement process, several specific data constraints apply. The record may include at most one direct link to a Certification Label, which identifies the specific set of norms, expectations, standards, or policies that the certificate addresses. Additionally, it can specify a maximum of one certification number, formatted as either a standard text string or a language-specific string, to serve as the unique identifier of the certificate. Finally, the certificate may provide at most one direct link to a Certifier, indicating the organization acting in the role responsible for verifying conformance and issuing the document.

selected.label: epo-shape:epo-AwardCriterionShape
selected.en: When defining an Award Criterion, which describes a requirement that a tender needs to resolve and on which it is evaluated and ranked, several specific data rules apply. You may provide at most one true or false value to indicate whether the award criteria are explicitly provided in the procurement documents. To classify the criterion, you can specify up to one award criterion type, which must be formatted as a direct link to a concept representing the category of the award criterion. Additionally, the record may include at most one fixed value, expressed as a decimal number to represent a constant amount. To clarify this number, you may also provide up to one fixed value type, which must be a specific identifier URL linking to a concept that defines the method for interpreting the fixed value, such as whether it pertains to a total or a unit.

selected.label: epo-shape:epo-MonetaryValueShape
selected.en: When defining a Monetary Value, which represents a number of monetary units specified using a given unit of currency (keeping in mind that in the pre-award phase of procurement, all monetary values are considered to exclude VAT based on Directive 2014/24/EU), specific data constraints must be followed. The record must specify exactly one amount value, formatted as a decimal number, to capture the numeric value of the amount including any decimals. It must also include exactly one currency, provided as a specific identifier URL linking to a concept that identifies the currency according to a standard code list. Additionally, the record may optionally include a currency code list agency ID to identify the agency that maintains the code list, a currency code list agency name, and a currency code list ID to indicate the concept scheme URI used for the list; all three of these optional details must be expressed as either standard or language-tagged strings.

selected.label: epo-shape:epo-cat-EnvironmentalEmissionInformationShape
selected.en: When defining Environmental Emission Information, which details the emissions related to a product, work, or service that are released into the environment, several strict data constraints apply. The record must specify exactly one environmental emission code using a specific identifier URL that links to a standardized concept. It must also include exactly one measure, provided as a direct link to a quantity that indicates the unit used for stating the size. Optionally, the emission information may contain a direct link to at most one abstract item, which represents an item, item request, or deliverable related to a procurement need. It may also include a direct link to at most one transport means, describing a particular vehicle or vessel used for the conveyance of goods or persons. Finally, the record may specify at most one calculation method to describe the formula used for obtaining values, such as monetary values, ranking scores, or criterion weighting; if provided, this method must be formatted as either a standard text string or a language-tagged string.

selected.label: epo-shape:epo-LotGroupAwardInformationShape
selected.en: When defining Lot Group Award Information to capture award details related to a given group of lots, you must provide exactly one direct link to the specific Lot Group it describes, which represents a combination of several lots used to conduct a comparative assessment of tenders. Additionally, the record may contain a single optional direct link to an approximate group framework agreement value, indicating the estimated monetary value of the lot group within the framework agreement, as well as a single optional direct link to the group framework agreement maximum value. If either of these framework agreement values is provided, it must be formatted as a specific identifier URL pointing to a Monetary Value record, which expresses the financial amount using a specified unit of currency.

selected.label: epo-shape:epo-ProcurementCriterionShape
selected.en: When defining a Procurement Criterion, which establishes a criterion specific to a procurement process, several data rules must be followed. You may provide at most one piece of additional information to offer supplementary data, which must be formatted as either a standard text string or a language-tagged string. The criterion can also be associated with specific limitations by linking to Constraint records; any such constraints must be provided as direct links to the respective limitation entities. If complex weighing methods, such as non-linear weighing or analytic hierarchy processes, are required because standard weighing cannot be expressed per criterion, you may include at most one formula. This formula must also be formatted as a standard text or language-tagged string to capture the mathematical equation or description. Finally, the criterion may specify at most one weight value type, which must be provided as a specific identifier URL pointing to a standardized Concept.

selected.label: epo-shape:epo-ful-ShipmentAgreementShape
selected.en: When defining a Shipment Agreement, which serves as the commercial agreement describing the items being shipped between the purchasing and supplying parties, specific acceptance rules must be followed. The agreement must specify at least one buyer who has accepted the terms, represented by a specific identifier URL linking directly to the Buyer, which is the agent that awards the contract or purchases the items. Furthermore, the record must include at least one seller who has accepted the agreement, also provided as a specific identifier URL pointing to the Seller, defined as the agent legally responsible for transferring the ownership of the procurement results, such as goods, services, or works, to the buyer.

selected.label: epo-shape:epo-BusinessShape
selected.en: When defining a Business, which represents a private law company registered in a national registry, several specific attributes may be recorded. You may identify the company's beneficial owners, referring to the natural persons who ultimately own or control the organization or on whose behalf a transaction is conducted. Each beneficial owner must be provided as a specific identifier URL linking to a record of a real, non-imaginary person. Additionally, you may specify at most one business size to categorize the enterprise based on its number of employees and turnover; this must be expressed as a direct link to a standardized concept. Finally, the business record may include a single true or false value to indicate whether it is a listed company. This indicator denotes if the entity is a public company listed on a stock exchange and subject to strict disclosure requirements, a detail often used in eForms when the nationality of the beneficial owner is not provided due to the market's existing transparency standards.

selected.label: ExistenzAuftragsnummerKaeuferKopf
selected.en: When defining details of an Invoice record, you must specify exactly one buyer order number formatted as a text string. Enforcing this single required text value ensures that the document header contains the necessary reference information, specifically the order number commonly identified as RFF+ON, and failing to provide it will trigger a validation error indicating that the supplier's order number is missing or extra from the header.

selected.label: GLNKaeufer
selected.en: When defining a Formal Organization, specific data curation rules apply based on the entity's role. If the organization is categorized as a Buyer, it must be assigned exactly one Global Location Number. To ensure data integrity and prevent system errors indicating that data element 3039 is missing for the NAD+BY segment, this location number must be formatted as a numeric integer that is exactly thirteen digits in length. Alternatively, if the organization is not designated with a Buyer role, this strict location number requirement does not apply.

selected.label: PLZLieferant
selected.en: When curating a Formal Organization record, specific constraints apply depending on its designated role. If the organization is explicitly categorized as a supplier, it is strictly required to provide exactly one postal code to satisfy the business requirement for data element 3251 within the NAD+SU segment. This supplier postal code must be recorded as a text string and cannot exceed a maximum length of nine characters. Alternatively, if the organization does not hold the supplier role, this specific postal code requirement does not apply.

selected.label: GLNRechnungsempfaenger
selected.en: When curating records for a Formal Organization, specific validation rules apply based on the entity's designated role. If the organization is classified as an invoice recipient, it is strictly required to provide exactly one Global Location Number to satisfy the requirements for data element 3039 within the NAD+IV segment. This location identifier must be formatted as a single integer that is exactly thirteen digits in length. If the organization does not serve in the invoice recipient role, this specific Global Location Number constraint does not apply, but failing to provide this thirteen-digit numeric identifier for an actual invoice recipient will result in a validation error indicating that the required specification is missing.

selected.label: LaengeLieferscheinnummer
selected.en: For any Invoice Details, the delivery note number must be formatted as a standard text string. Because this field represents the supplier's order number, specifically the RFF+DQ reference, it is strictly limited in size to prevent system errors where the value is too long. Therefore, the provided text must never exceed a maximum length of 35 characters.

selected.label: UmsatzsteuernummerKaeufer
selected.en: When defining a Formal Organization, strict data rules govern the presence of tax information based on the entity's function. If the organization is classified specifically as a Buyer Role, it is mandatory to provide exactly one VAT identifier, and this value must not exceed fourteen characters in length. The validation logic dictates that the organization must either not be categorized as a buyer at all, or it must fulfill this exact VAT identifier requirement. Failure to provide this required data for a buyer will trigger a system alert stating that the buyer's VAT number is missing from the record. Alternatively, if the organization is not designated with a Buyer role, this strict VAT identifier requirement does not apply.

selected.label: StrasseLieferant
selected.en: When defining a Formal Organization, specific data entry rules apply based on the organization's designated role. If the organization is categorized specifically as a supplier, it must include exactly one street address formatted as a text string that does not exceed 35 characters in length. This conditional requirement ensures proper record completeness, as omitting this information will trigger a validation error indicating that data element 3042 is missing for the NAD+SU segment, which strictly mandates the specification of the supplier's street. However, if the formal organization is not classified under the supplier role, it is entirely exempt from this specific street address constraint.

selected.label: ExistenzDatumLieferscheinnummer
selected.en: When curating details for an Invoice record, you must specify exactly one date associated with the delivery note number. This mandatory date must be formatted as a text string. It is critical to include this single required value, as its absence will trigger a system alert stating that the date of the supplier's order number, specifically the RFF+DQ reference, is missing from the document.

selected.label: PLZKaeufer
selected.en: When curating records for a Formal Organization, specific validation rules apply to ensure the proper specification of a buyer's postal code. If the organization is explicitly designated with a Buyer Role, the record must include exactly one postal code formatted as a text string with a maximum length of nine characters. If the organization does not function as a buyer, this postal code constraint does not apply. Enforcing this rule ensures that data element 3251 is correctly populated for the NAD+BY segment, and any omission for a recognized buyer will be flagged as a missing postal code error.

selected.label: FormalNameLieferant
selected.en: When defining a Formal Organization within the data model, specific curation rules apply to ensure the proper identification of suppliers, specifically addressing the requirement for data element 3036 in the NAD+SU segment. If the organization is categorized under a Supplier Role, it is strictly required to include exactly one formal name. This formal name must be provided as a standard text string and cannot exceed a maximum length of 35 characters. If the organization is not designated as a supplier, it is exempt from this specific naming constraint.

selected.label: meta:NotRoleShape
selected.en: An entity type or a function cannot be categorized as a specific type of role.

selected.label: meta:NotEntityTypeShape
selected.en: Functions and roles must not be classified as subcategories of an entity type.

selected.label: meta:NotFunctionShape
selected.en: An entity type or a role must never be classified as a subclass of a function.

selected.label: meta:TopShape
selected.en: Every top class must be categorized as exactly one of three things: an entity type, a function, or a role. Any top class can be linked to other concepts through exact, close, related, broader, or narrower matches, and can be marked as a homonym. Beyond these matching links, each category is strictly limited in what characteristics it can have. An entity type may only include a label, entity type components, and information about what it is based on, while specifically ignoring traits like software products, typical features, supported functions, or communication with other components. A function is restricted to having a label, function components, and relationships showing that it uses, updates, increases, or decreases an entity type. Similarly, a role is limited to having a label, role components, and details about its duties, such as being involved in a task, being responsible for another role, function, or entity type, or having the authority to approve functions and entity types.

selected.label: meta:RoleShape
selected.en: Every role must have at least one human-readable name. A role is strictly limited to a specific set of allowed relationships and cannot have any other custom attributes. Specifically, a role can be responsible for another role, a function, or an entity type. It may also approve functions or entity types, be involved in tasks, or include other roles as components.
